summary:
YoutubeDemo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GffKs_kmG94

SOMA (Space Operations Medical Assistant) is an offline, local on-device voice assistant that enables astronauts to monitor and log health data in hands-free mode with visual feedback during deep space missions without Earth communications reliance. Multilingual, ability to add more languages to cator to multiple demographics crew (two way input output stt and tts). Built for the 2026 NASA International Space Apps Challenge.

Features: Multilingual TTS, STT, hands-free, offline, voice assistant, telemedicine, linux OS (ability to ship to multiple platform)

What is SOMA?
Offline, local, on-device medical monitoring and logging voice assistant.
Lets astronauts log and monitor health hands-free with no dependence on internet/Earth networks.
Crew speak naturally in English (more languages can be added later)
Records heart rate, sleep, mood, and symptoms (As a proof of concept MVP but can be connected with existing SOP)
Color coded body map, live trend charts, NASA-style crew health table. (proof of concept)
Print / Print-to-PDF export built in. For saving outside the web browser or terminal.
General self-care info with red-flag guidance.

Impact:
Keeps a usable health record where evacuation, telemedicine, communication are impossible.
Hands-free logging suits gloved / suited operations, Color + trends let any crew member triage at a glance
Log format mirrors Apollo / ISS crew-status practice.
details:
SOMA (Space Operations Medical Assistant) is an offline, on-device, medical monitoring and logging, voice assistant that lets astronauts log and monitor health hands-free in multiple languaes, during deep space missions with no dependency on Earth network connection/communications systems. Crew speak naturally in english (more languages can be added). SOMA records heart rate, sleep, mood, and symptoms, shows a color coded body map, live trend charts, and a NASA style crew health table with print, print to PDF export, plus general self care info with red-flag guidance.

How does it work? : 100% local tech stack run on a Linux OS, using localhost url http://127.0.0.1:8080/ any web browser without internet: whisper.cpp for speech-to-text, Qwen3.5-4B (llama.cpp) for the SI assistant, Paradee TTS local neural voices for speech, all behind a same-origin Python proxy. No cloud, no data leaves the device. Frontend is plain HTML/JS with inline SVG charts (no dependencies, works offline). Vitals thresholds come from a curated nasa-vitals.json; self-care text from a curated lookup file (general info only, never doses, always "call the flight surgeon" on red flags).

Impact: Keeps a usable health record when evacuation and telemedicine are impossible (Mars: up to ~22-min one-way delay). Hands-free logging fits suited/gloved ops; color + trends let any crew member triage at a glance; the log format mirrors Apollo/ISS crew-status practice so flight surgeons get familiar data.

Tools used: JavaScript/HTML/CSS, Python (proxy/server), whisper.cpp, llama.cpp, Qwen3.5-4B Q3_K_M, Paradee TTS, Git.

Gamification: Game-style pre-flight gate (systems/mic/voice check), clickable astronaut body tied to live readings with deltas vs previous log, SI-assisted code clearly labeled.

Factors: Offline-first (deep-space delay), low-end hardware (i5, no GPU needed), safety (no diagnosis, no dosages, red-flag escalation), accessibility (voice + typed fallback, hands-free audio that needs no tap per reply). Health history.
